Definition: from G1223 and the genitive case of G3956; through all time, i.e. (adverbially) constantly:--alway(-s), continually.
BiblicalUsage: This entry is not one word but two standing together, through and all, and the Greek text never joins them into a single word. Luke says the disciples were continually in the temple praising God, and Peter quotes the psalm that the Lord is always before his face, and in both places the two words together mean always.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that always is the right way to read these verses; the disciples did not visit the temple now and then; they lived there in praise, and the Lord was not before David sometimes, but continually.
